chant.letra:
[Leader]
Volleyball — play, go or do?
[Kids]
PLAY! We play volleyball!

[Leader]
Skating — play, go or do?
[Kids]
GO! We go skating!

[Leader]
And athletics?
[Kids]
DO! We do athletics!

[Leader]
And who wins the prize?
[Kids]
The team! The whole team!

[All]
Golf and sledging, snowboarding —
race and score and champion!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
You play a game with a ball,
you go where the verb ends in '-ing'.
You do the ones without a ball
and that's the whole strange thing.

[Chorus]
Play volleyball, go skating,
do the race and try!
Team and score and prize and champion —
reach a little higher every time!

[Verse 2]
A balanced diet, an exercise routine,
sleep hygiene at night.
The champion is not the fastest —
it's the one who does it right.

[Chorus]
Play volleyball, go skating,
do the race and try!
Team and score and prize and champion —
reach a little higher every time!

[Bridge]
Snowboarding, sledging, golf —
three more and you know them all.

[Chorus]
Play volleyball, go skating,
do the race and try!
Team and score and prize and champion —
reach a little higher every time!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What were you doing at four?
[Kids]
We were practising! In the gym!

[Leader]
What was Ingrid doing?
[Kids]
She was swimming! In the pool!

[Leader]
What was Diego doing?
[Kids]
He was shouting! From the court!

[Leader]
And then?
[Kids]
The whistle! Everybody stopped!

[All]
Changing room and slip and fall —
carry on, that's not the end at all!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
We were practising at six,
the pool was almost empty.
Ingrid was carrying the bags
and Oliver had plenty.

[Chorus]
I was, you were, they were doing —
something in the middle of the day!
Then the whistle went and stopped it
and it all just blew away!

[Verse 2]
Maya slipped beside the court
while she was looking at the sky.
It wasn't terrifying, it was funny,
and unforgettable — that's why.

[Chorus]
I was, you were, they were doing —
something in the middle of the day!
Then the whistle went and stopped it
and it all just blew away!

[Bridge]
Breathtaking and rewarding:
two long words for one short hour.

[Chorus]
I was, you were, they were doing —
something in the middle of the day!
Then the whistle went and stopped it
and it all just blew away!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
My birthday — in or on?
[Kids]
ON! On the third of March!

[Leader]
The holidays — in or on?
[Kids]
IN! In August!

[Leader]
The first snow — in or on?
[Kids]
IN! In December!

[Leader]
And the leaves?
[Kids]
In autumn! Every autumn!

[All]
January, February, April too —
October, spring — a century through!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
In January the harbour freezes,
in February the light comes back.
On the third of March it's Ingrid's birthday
and the ice begins to crack.

[Chorus]
IN a month and ON a date,
IN a season, that's the rule!
April, August, October, December —
and the spring that empties school!

[Verse 2]
In autumn Sven tells the same story
he has told for fifty years.
A century ago, he says,
and everybody cheers.

[Chorus]
IN a month and ON a date,
IN a season, that's the rule!
April, August, October, December —
and the spring that empties school!

[Bridge]
Not 'in the third of March'.
One small word and it's all right.

[Chorus]
IN a month and ON a date,
IN a season, that's the rule!
April, August, October, December —
and the spring that empties school!

18.gramatica: quarter past / half past / quarter to

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What time is it?
[Kids]
Quarter past eight! Nearly late!

[Leader]
What time is it?
[Kids]
Half past nine! We're doing fine!

[Leader]
What time is it?
[Kids]
Quarter to one! Almost done!

[Leader]
And now?
[Kids]
Midday! Midday exactly!

[All]
Minute, alarm and hurry, late —
midnight comes and we can't wait!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The alarm went off at midnight
because Oliver set it wrong.
At quarter past six he was still asleep
and half past seven came along.

[Chorus]
Quarter past, half past, quarter to —
hurry up, it's nearly nine!
Early, late or right on time,
the minute hand won't wait in line!

[Verse 2]
At midday the bell goes twice,
at one o'clock we eat.
A minute is a little thing
until you're on the street.

[Chorus]
Quarter past, half past, quarter to —
hurry up, it's nearly nine!
Early, late or right on time,
the minute hand won't wait in line!

[Bridge]
Past goes forward, 'to' goes back:
half the clock and that's the knack.

[Chorus]
Quarter past, half past, quarter to —
hurry up, it's nearly nine!
Early, late or right on time,
the minute hand won't wait in line!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What came first?
[Kids]
The wind! The wind began to blow!

[Leader]
And then?
[Kids]
The lightning! Then the thunder!

[Leader]
And then?
[Kids]
The flood! The road went under!

[Leader]
And in the morning?
[Kids]
The sun! The sun began to shine!

[All]
Fog and ice and wet and dry —
the storm went out across the sky!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The wind blew hard on Saturday,
the lightning lit the bay.
The thunder followed seven seconds later
and the fog rolled in to stay.

[Chorus]
Storm and lightning, ice and flood,
wet today and dry tomorrow!
After the thunder comes the shine —
no weather lasts, not even sorrow!

[Verse 2]
The flood took half the lower road,
the ice took half the rest.
We reduce waste and we clear the drains
and hope we've done our best.

[Chorus]
Storm and lightning, ice and flood,
wet today and dry tomorrow!
After the thunder comes the shine —
no weather lasts, not even sorrow!

[Bridge]
It blew, it shone, it froze, it poured:
the past simple keeps the record.

[Chorus]
Storm and lightning, ice and flood,
wet today and dry tomorrow!
After the thunder comes the shine —
no weather lasts, not even sorrow!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
The spoon — what's it made of?
[Kids]
Metal! It's made of metal!

[Leader]
The window?
[Kids]
Glass! It's made of glass!

[Leader]
The jumper?
[Kids]
Wool! It's made of wool!

[Leader]
And the ring?
[Kids]
Gold! Or silver! Or both!

[All]
Wood and paper, plastic, stone —
card and cloth and all we own!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The bridge is made of stone and metal,
the boat is made of wood.
The window's made of glass and silence
and it does exactly what it should.

[Chorus]
What's it made of? Say it simply:
wood or metal, glass or wool!
Paper, plastic, gold and silver —
every thing is made of something!

[Verse 2]
The plastic lasts four hundred years,
the paper lasts a week.
The card goes in the blue bin
and the plastic makes us think.

[Chorus]
What's it made of? Say it simply:
wood or metal, glass or wool!
Paper, plastic, gold and silver —
every thing is made of something!

[Bridge]
Made OF, not made FROM, not made WITH.
One small word — and that's the myth.

[Chorus]
What's it made of? Say it simply:
wood or metal, glass or wool!
Paper, plastic, gold and silver —
every thing is made of something!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What's over the hill?
[Kids]
A waterfall! A big waterfall!

[Leader]
What's behind the wood?
[Kids]
A cave! A dark, cold cave!

[Leader]
What's beside the stream?
[Kids]
Our tent! And the fire!

[Leader]
And above it all?
[Kids]
The sky! The whole sky!

[All]
Island, path and hill and wood —
there it is, and it is good!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
There is an island in the lake
and a path that leads around.
There are three hills behind the wood
and hardly any sound.

[Chorus]
There is a cave, there are the stars,
there's a waterfall that never stops!
The tent, the fire, the open sky —
and the stream that runs across the rocks!

[Verse 2]
We built the fire before it darkened,
Maya named the constellations.
Kili landed in the water
to enormous celebrations.

[Chorus]
There is a cave, there are the stars,
there's a waterfall that never stops!
The tent, the fire, the open sky —
and the stream that runs across the rocks!

[Bridge]
One thing 'is'. More things 'are'.
Countryside, and not too far.

[Chorus]
There is a cave, there are the stars,
there's a waterfall that never stops!
The tent, the fire, the open sky —
and the stream that runs across the rocks!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Which is the longest?
[Kids]
The river! The longest river!

[Leader]
Which is the deepest?
[Kids]
The ocean! The deepest ocean!

[Leader]
Which is the widest?
[Kids]
The mouth! Where it meets the sea!

[Leader]
How many kilometres?
[Kids]
Thousands! Thousands and thousands!

[All]
North and south and boat and bridge —
follow the water to the ridge!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
A river starts up in the mountains
as a stream you'd hardly see.
It runs a thousand kilometres
and it ends up in the sea.

[Chorus]
The longest, the deepest, the widest of all —
follow it north, follow it south!
Under the bridge and past the boat,
all the way down to the mouth!

[Verse 2]
Maya measured on the map
with a ruler and a string.
Two thousand, seven hundred, forty —
and that's a serious thing.

[Chorus]
The longest, the deepest, the widest of all —
follow it north, follow it south!
Under the bridge and past the boat,
all the way down to the mouth!

[Bridge]
The ocean holds them every one,
and never says which river won.

[Chorus]
The longest, the deepest, the widest of all —
follow it north, follow it south!
Under the bridge and past the boat,
all the way down to the mouth!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Look at that!
[Kids]
What a strange planet!

[Leader]
And that!
[Kids]
What a bright star!

[Leader]
And that!
[Kids]
What a fast rocket!

[Leader]
And who is inside?
[Kids]
An astronaut! Maybe an alien!

[All]
Moon and Earth and spaceship, round —
what a sky above the ground!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
What a strange and quiet planet,
what a very distant star.
The rocket left on Tuesday morning
and it isn't very far.

[Chorus]
What a sky! What a moon!
What a round and turning Earth!
Astronaut and spaceship, space —
what a place to have your birth!

[Verse 2]
Maya says there might be water
on a moon we haven't named.
If there's water there is maybe life,
and nobody's ashamed.

[Chorus]
What a sky! What a moon!
What a round and turning Earth!
Astronaut and spaceship, space —
what a place to have your birth!

[Bridge]
An alien would look at us
and say the very same.

[Chorus]
What a sky! What a moon!
What a round and turning Earth!
Astronaut and spaceship, space —
what a place to have your birth!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Grum — what has he got?
[Kids]
Three eyes! And he's very hairy!

[Leader]
Zog — what has he got?
[Kids]
One eye! And two long arms!

[Leader]
Zip — what has he got?
[Kids]
Four eyes! And he's small and round!

[Leader]
Who is the tallest?
[Kids]
Zog! And Zip is the shortest!

[All]
Curly, straight and fair and dark —
old and young, they're quite a mark!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Grum has got green hair, all curly,
Zog has got no hair at all.
Zip is short and rather round
and the youngest of them all.

[Chorus]
He has got, she has got,
curly, straight and dark and fair!
Tall or short, thin or fat,
old or young — describe them there!

[Verse 2]
The album has a hundred photos
and in none of them they blink.
Four eyes never close together —
at least that's what they think.

[Chorus]
He has got, she has got,
curly, straight and dark and fair!
Tall or short, thin or fat,
old or young — describe them there!

[Bridge]
Describing isn't laughing at.
You say what's there, and that is that.

[Chorus]
He has got, she has got,
curly, straight and dark and fair!
Tall or short, thin or fat,
old or young — describe them there!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What is Ingrid like?
[Kids]
Brave! And very ambitious!

[Leader]
What is Oliver like?
[Kids]
Funny! Creative! And noisy!

[Leader]
What is Maya like?
[Kids]
Clever! Careful! Patient!

[Leader]
And what are we all?
[Kids]
Kind! Polite! Reliable!

[All]
Quiet, generous, lazy, friendly —
stubborn too, and that's us plainly!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Ingrid's brave and rather stubborn,
which is often the same thing.
Diego's friendly with a microphone
and noisy when he sings.

[Chorus]
Clever, kind and careful, patient,
funny, quiet, generous, polite!
But the word I'd want most of all
is reliable — that's right!

[Verse 2]
Oliver is creative,
Maya is ambitious too.
Lazy on a Sunday morning —
and honestly, aren't you?

[Chorus]
Clever, kind and careful, patient,
funny, quiet, generous, polite!
But the word I'd want most of all
is reliable — that's right!

[Bridge]
Being clever's luck. Being kind's a choice.
Choose the second with your voice.

[Chorus]
Clever, kind and careful, patient,
funny, quiet, generous, polite!
But the word I'd want most of all
is reliable — that's right!

26.unidad: Have you ever met a famous person?

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Have you ever flown?
[Kids]
Yes! I have flown twice!

[Leader]
Have you ever swum in the sea?
[Kids]
Yes! I have swum in winter!

[Leader]
Have you ever climbed a mountain?
[Kids]
Never! I have never climbed one!

[Leader]
Have you ever met somebody famous?
[Kids]
Once! In a queue! Once!

[All]
Met and flown and swum and been —
ever, never, in between!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Have you ever met a famous person?
Diego says he nearly did.
He has flown to seven countries
and has never lost a bid.

[Chorus]
Have you ever? Have you never?
Somewhere in your life so far!
Met and flown and swum and climbed —
that's the story of who you are!

[Verse 2]
Maya's never climbed a mountain,
Ingrid's climbed them all.
Oliver has swum the harbour
in October, in the squall.

[Chorus]
Have you ever? Have you never?
Somewhere in your life so far!
Met and flown and swum and climbed —
that's the story of who you are!

[Bridge]
It doesn't matter when it was.
It matters that it was, because.

[Chorus]
Have you ever? Have you never?
Somewhere in your life so far!
Met and flown and swum and climbed —
that's the story of who you are!

27.gramatica: present perfect with just / already / yet

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What has just happened?
[Kids]
The train has just arrived!

[Leader]
Have they finished?
[Kids]
Already! They've already finished!

[Leader]
Has the news come?
[Kids]
Not yet! It hasn't come yet!

[Leader]
And the window?
[Kids]
Broken! Somebody has broken it!

[All]
Just and already, not yet —
it happened and we feel it yet!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The train has just arrived at platform two,
the letter has already come.
The story hasn't finished yet
and nothing here is done.

[Chorus]
Just, already, not yet —
three small words that hold the day!
It has happened, it still matters,
and it hasn't gone away!

[Verse 2]
Kili has arrived with postcards,
one is broken at the edge.
He has already dropped the others
somewhere off the ledge.

[Chorus]
Just, already, not yet —
three small words that hold the day!
It has happened, it still matters,
and it hasn't gone away!

[Bridge]
'I finished' is a closed door.
'I have finished' — there's still more.

[Chorus]
Just, already, not yet —
three small words that hold the day!
It has happened, it still matters,
and it hasn't gone away!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
They were tired, so…
[Kids]
they went to sleep!

[Leader]
They went to sleep because…
[Kids]
they were tired!

[Leader]
She was hungry, so…
[Kids]
she ate everything!

[Leader]
He was afraid because…
[Kids]
the cave was dark!

[All]
Thirsty, bored and excited too —
'so' is what, 'because' is why!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
They were tired, so they stopped,
they stopped because the day was long.
She was thirsty, so she drank,
and both of those are strong.

[Chorus]
'So' comes after, 'because' comes first —
one is the reason, one is what!
Tired, hungry, bored, excited —
say them both and join the lot!

[Verse 2]
He was afraid because it thundered,
so he counted to eleven.
The reason and the thing that followed:
two halves of the same heaven.

[Chorus]
'So' comes after, 'because' comes first —
one is the reason, one is what!
Tired, hungry, bored, excited —
say them both and join the lot!

[Bridge]
Give the reason and you're understood.
That's the difference — and it's good.

[Chorus]
'So' comes after, 'because' comes first —
one is the reason, one is what!
Tired, hungry, bored, excited —
say them both and join the lot!
